basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost per part at its Braga plant and put the improvements in place?

sub_questions.question: What is the conversion cost per part today, and where does it arise across the plant's production lines?
Which improvements can reduce conversion cost per part, and by how much each?
How are the chosen improvements put in place at the plant and kept running in daily operations?
What conversion cost per part do the implemented improvements show in the plant's cost data?

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phase_work.why: One plant is diagnosed on the floor, with COO and Plant Director interviews alongside; the estimate is within the archetype's 3-6 weeks.

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data

phase_work.why: One plant is the pilot site, changed across its three lines; the estimate is within the archetype's 8-16 weeks.

sizing.levers: Limiting Implementation to the changes on one production line instead of all three would shorten the engagement most.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish the conversion cost per part at the Braga plant and size the improvements that would reduce it.

gate.label: Initiatives go/no-go
gate.decision: Which sized improvements go into implementation at the Braga plant?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Put the approved improvements in place at the Braga plant and show the reduction in conversion cost per part.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the final results: cost per part down and improvements running at the plant?

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; the 13-16 weeks are an estimate from one plant, to be confirmed before this becomes a quote.
Plant and line counts (one plant, three production lines) come from public research and need the client's confirmation.
Implementation uses the middle of an 8-12 week estimate; changes needed on all three lines in sequence would push it to the top.
Implementation holds one pilot-site unit and no rollout waves, since the profile shows a single plant; confirm there is no second site.
No Measurement phase: results tracking against the baseline runs inside Implementation, so there is no separate tracking period after launch.
